papers.title: ALY688 Protects Against Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Direct Effects and Rab8a-Dependent Extracellular Vesicles.
papers.summary: Synthetic adiponectin receptor agonist peptide ALY688 reduced myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model: lowered troponin-I, cardiomyocyte death and infarct size while preserving function. It restored autophagic flux, mitigated ROS and apoptosis, and increased Rab8a-dependent extracellular vesicles conferring cardioprotective effects.

papers.title: Pharmacological Inhibition of Small Extracellular Vesicle Secretion by ALK5i SD-208 via Lysosomal Rerouting of CD63+ Compartments.
papers.summary: ALK5 inhibitor SD-208 suppressed small EV secretion independently of its TGF-beta-Smad anti-fibrotic activity by diverting CD63+ multivesicular bodies to LAMP1+ lysosomes. It is proposed as a small-molecule tool to interrogate secretory-versus-degradative MVB fate and control EV secretion in disease.

papers.title: Host-to-Pathogen Transfer of Neutrophil Components via Extracellular Vesicles Shields Candida albicans From Immune Attack in Human Blood.
papers.summary: Neutrophil-derived EVs, enriched in antimicrobial proteins and surface markers, bound Candida albicans complement-dependently, partly via CR3. Despite antimicrobial cargo they did not impair growth; EV coating reduced phagocytosis, preserving an extracellular viable fungal population in human blood.

papers.title: Selective Packaging of miR-22 and miR-29 Orthologues into Extracellular Vesicles of the Porcine Whipworm Trichuris Suis.
papers.summary: Trichuris suis EVs did not suppress LPS-induced TNF production, unlike non-vesicular ESP. Adult EVs selectively enriched miR-22-3p and miR-29-3p orthologues that downregulated conserved oncogenic targets in colon cancer cells, suggesting EV-mediated modulation of host tissue remodeling.

papers.title: Pyroptosis-Amplified Decoy Nanovesicles Orchestrate Pyroptotic Antigen Explosion and Endogenous Immune Revitalization for Potentiating Tumour Immunotherapy.
papers.summary: Pyroptosis-amplified decoy nanovesicles combined checkpoint blockade (PD-1/PD-L1, SIRPalpha/CD47) with cytosolic decitabine and LPS to trigger gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis and antigen release. This reversed T-cell exhaustion and mounted durable anti-tumor immunity in melanoma, breast and colon cancer models.

papers.title: Reduced astroglial-synapse coverage on cortical non-engram cells shapes remote memory strength.
papers.summary: Using a genetically targeted approach (Astro-GRASP), remote memory strength in prelimbic cortex was shaped by astrocyte selective retraction from non-engram synapses, not engram synapses. Depleting ezrin reduced local astrocyte-synapse coverage and enhanced remote memory, highlighting a role for astrocytic remodeling in consolidation.

papers.title: Ceramide transfer protein regulates G-protein-coupled phospholipase signalling in photoreceptors.
papers.summary: Loss of Drosophila dCert elevated short-chain ceramides and reduced phosphoethanolamine ceramide in photoreceptors, impairing light responses and PIP2 resynthesis after phospholipase C stimulation, associated with reduced ER-plasma membrane contact-site density. CERT thus regulates G-protein-coupled PLC signaling in vivo.

papers.title: Reexamining the activation mechanisms of adhesion G protein-coupled receptors.
papers.summary: This review reexamines adhesion GPCR activation, arguing the canonical tethered-agonist mechanism is insufficient. It advances an ECR-dependent allosteric model offering reversible, tunable signaling responsive to pulling and compressive forces, proposing a unified context-dependent framework integrating all activation modes for therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Metabolic shifts driven by host-microbial interactions.
papers.summary: Review presenting microbial metabolism as an organizing principle of host-microbiota symbiosis. Microbiota-derived metabolites (short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, tryptophan indoles, sphingolipids, gaseous products) signal via nuclear receptors, transcriptional regulators and redox pathways to control host energy homeostasis and immunity, with therapies targeting microbial metabolism.

papers.title: Loss of Miro1 drives cardiac and mitochondrial dysfunction exacerbated by metabolic stress.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: Cardiac-specific Miro1 knockout mice developed mild diastolic/systolic dysfunction, hypertrophy and fibrosis, with aberrant mitochondrial respiration, elevated H2O2, disrupted cristae and impaired mitophagy. Heterozygotes rapidly developed heart failure on high-fat diet plus L-NAME. Miro1 is identified as a regulator of cardiac mitochondrial morphology.

papers.title: Biallelic titin truncation disrupts sarcomere assembly and function in patient-derived iPSC cardiomyocytes.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: In iPSC-cardiomyocytes from a biallelic titin-truncation dilated cardiomyopathy patient, only the longest TTNtv was translated and incorporated into the sarcomere. Subtle shortening of A-bands led to reduced force and contractility, with sarcomeres stretched by neighbors, implicating inefficient sarcomere assembly in cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Structural and functional insights into Pseudomonas aeruginosa ApaH, a diadenosine tetraphosphatase crucial for bacterial virulence.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Integrated biochemical, structural, computational and phenotypic work defines P. aeruginosa ApaH, a manganese-dependent diadenosine tetraphosphatase, and links its catalytic activity directly to in vivo virulence. With no eukaryotic ApaH homologs, it is proposed as a selective antivirulence drug target.

papers.title: Catalytic architecture and cyclase-mediated dimerization of a newly identified class III-c lanthipeptide synthetase.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Cryo-EM revealed class III-c LanKC synthetase TherKC assembles as a homodimer exclusively via cyclase-cyclase interactions centered on Arg685, distinct from all characterized LanKC enzymes. Disrupting that interface abolishes dimerization and reduces stability while retaining catalysis, defining conserved cyclase residues for dehydration-cyclization coupling.

papers.title: Viral PDZ target sequences are not inherently more promiscuous than those derived from endogenous target proteins.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Fluorescence anisotropy measurements of 7 endogenous and 7 viral PDZ-binding motifs across 8 class I PDZ domains found no significant difference in relative promiscuity. Viral origin alone does not explain promiscuity; recognition is driven by widely favorable modulator residues at sequence hotspots.

papers.title: Structure and conformational dynamics of the Pseudomonas CbrA transceptor.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A cryo-EM structure of the Pseudomonas transceptor CbrA defined its SLC5-STAC domains and histidine binding, with molecular dynamics revealing proton-gradient-driven conformational changes enabling histidine transport. The upstream peptide CbrX formed a stable complex but was not essential for growth on histidine.

papers.title: A multiplex tissue resource for high-resolution spatial protein profiling in the Human Protein Atlas.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: The Human Protein Atlas version 25 multiplex tissue resource analyzed 1,106 proteins with eight antibody panels across nine tissue settings, resolving cell states and subcellular compartments including spermatogenesis stages, ciliary compartments and nephron segments. It provides high-resolution spatial context for protein expression.

papers.title: Multimerization of a rationally designed nanobody for enhanced avidity toward Aβ42 oligomers.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Multimerizing the conformation-specific single-domain antibody DesabO, which binds Abeta42 oligomers, increased avidity toward those oligomers. Multimeric variants inhibited Abeta42 aggregation at concentrations where the monomer was ineffective, with the SB175 trimer best, offering a route to Alzheimer's diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.title: MAXTIA: A high-throughput platform for rapid functional epitope mapping by kinetic screening of mutant libraries.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: MAXTIA combines cell-free protein synthesis with high-throughput surface plasmon resonance to map functional epitopes by kinetic screening of up to 384 variants in ~3 days, returning KD, kon and koff. Alanine-scanning of nanobody N1 against NP2 PTX identified a functional epitope matching the crystal interface.

papers.title: Disulfide engineering of the FANCM-MHF complex reveals constraints on crosslink design in symmetric oligomers.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Structure-guided disulfide engineering of the FANCM-MHF complex showed geometric plausibility alone does not predict crosslinking specificity in symmetric oligomers. Q74C formed the intended FANCM-MHF2 disulfide enabling crystallization of the intact heteropentamer, whereas L77C favored a competing MHF2-MHF2 disulfide.

papers.title: Donor-induced conformational gating and substrate-assisted catalysis in α-1,3-galactosyltransferase.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Alanine-scanning of the C-terminal loop of bovine alpha1,3-galactosyltransferase identified Lys359, Tyr361 and Arg365 as critical for donor binding and catalysis. Donor (UDP-Gal) binding induces an ordered C-terminus that pre-organizes the active site, supporting coupling of conformational gating with catalysis in GT-A enzymes.

papers.title: A protein chaperone can stabilize the intein-containing precursor to indirectly promote protein splicing.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Intein splicing of M. smegmatis DnaB is temperature-sensitive. GroEL overexpression increases the pool of unspliced precursor (rather than directly promoting splicing), yielding more overall splicing. First description of a chaperone promoting protein splicing, with implications for intein-based protein engineering.

papers.title: Adaptation of OXPHOS biogenesis to cellular requirements.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Review of metabolic regulation of mitochondrial OXPHOS biogenesis. Cytochrome c oxidase assembly is controlled at multiple steps through mitochondrial translation, proteolytic removal of unassembled subunits and supercomplex formation, with tissue-specific factors tuning efficiency, limiting ROS and supporting context-specific metabolism.

papers.title: 4-Ethyl phenyl sulfate binding to human serum albumin.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Studied 4-ethylphenyl sulfate binding to human serum albumin by STD-NMR, ITC, docking and MD. Two interactions were identified at Sudlow sites I and II (Ka1 6.62e5 and Ka2 2.71e4 M-1) without gross unfolding, informing strategies for protein-bound uremic toxin removal in kidney failure.

papers.title: Pro4S: Prediction of protein solubility by fusing sequence, structure, and surface.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Pro4S, a multimodal protein solubility predictor fusing sequence, structure and surface descriptors via contrastive learning, outperformed state-of-the-art predictors. In de novo design it reduced non-expressed proteins by 52.7% while retaining 96.7% of highly expressed ones, serving as an upfront screening tool for protein engineering.

papers.title: Peroxynitrite-induced structural remodeling and aggregation of hemoglobin under nitroxidative stress.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Peroxynitrite exposure drove hemoglobin remodeling: at high oxidant loads alpha-helix content collapsed to 8.81% with beta-sheet enriched to 71.18%, forming amorphous/oligomeric aggregates rather than canonical amyloid fibrils (no crystalline order). PN lowered the nucleation barrier for thermally driven aggregation.

papers.title: A cryptic allosteric pocket shapes isoform-selective inhibition of human malic enzymes.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Matched kinetic profiles of malic enzymes ME1-3 showed NPD-389 occupies a conserved metal-coordinating active-site pose (non-selective). Flavianic acid engages a cryptic pocket accessible only in mitochondrial ME2/ME3, locking an open inactive conformation with isoform-specific allosteric responses. Conformational dynamics, not catalytic-site sequence, generate isoform selectivity.

papers.title: The C117D oxidation mimic reveals the monomeric structure of SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Oxidation mimic C117D rendered SARS-CoV-2 main protease monomeric and destabilized (100-fold lower activity), with ~40-degree rotation of domain III, disordered termini and an unwound oxyanion loop. It provides a high-resolution monomeric Mpro structure and points to dimerization-interface targeting for allosteric inhibitor design.

papers.title: Graph identification of proteins in tomograms (GRIP-Tomo) 2.0: Topologically aware classification for proteins.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: GRIP-Tomo 2.0 is a graph/network machine-learning pipeline using topological features to distinguish proteins from noise in cryo-electron tomography. It achieves over 90% accuracy on synthetic and over 80% on real datasets, advancing automated protein detection for visual proteomics.

papers.title: Identification of a key water molecule involved in the macrophage migration inhibitory factor-catalyzed tautomerization of para-hydroxyphenylpyruvate using neutron crystallography.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A 2.5-angstrom neutron crystal structure of MIF bound to HPP revealed the position of a water molecule supplying the proton for enol tautomerization and confirmed active-site Lys32 charge. It corroborates the proposed catalytic mechanism (N-terminal Pro-1 abstracting a proton), aiding MIF inhibitor screening.

papers.title: Quaternary structures of Streptococcus pneumoniae nucleoside diphosphate kinase: From hexamers to supramolecular assemblies.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Crystal structures of Streptococcus pneumoniae nucleoside diphosphate kinase (apo 1.2 Angstrom; ADP-vanadate 3.4 Angstrom) showed a hexameric assembly stabilized by the extended Kpn-loop (Tm ~76 C). R28A destabilized the hexamer (>20 C drop), and size-exclusion chromatography and mass photometry revealed hexamer/dodecamer/higher-order equilibria, with cryo-EM resolving dodecamers.

papers.title: The modular evolution of multiheme cytochromes c bucks the general trend observed in most proteins.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Analysis of all characterized multiheme cytochromes c shows they evolve by fusion and fission of modules. Heme addition occurs exclusively by integrating heme-binding peptides, while heme loss involves peptide loss plus point mutations, and heme-motif loss is disproportionately N-terminal — bucking the general trend of N-terminal conservation.

papers.title: Investigating enzyme function by geometric matching of catalytic motifs.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A library of 6,780 catalytic-site templates (from 762 M-CSA mechanisms) was searched with the JESS geometric-matching algorithm plus RMSD/orientation filters. Structural matching was more sensitive than sequence-based methods for distant homology and uncovered divergent/convergent active sites; provided as the enzymm Python module and web server.

papers.title: Engineered antibodies preserve structural and functional recognition of Plasmodium falciparum circumsporozoite protein.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Crystal and cryo-EM structures of engineered anti-PfCSP malaria antibodies mam01, ms-1805 and 7088 in complex with PfCSP regions showed 7088 has an extended CDRL3:10 loop. Framework engineering (half-life extension, manufacture) preserved key hydrogen bonds and binding affinity while retaining antigen recognition.

papers.title: Predicting membrane protein localization by deep learning on structure and chemistry.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: GPSForTMDs, a graph neural network trained on experimental membrane protein structures, predicts the native membrane environment of transmembrane domains. It performs competitively with sequence-based methods and exceptionally for some membrane categories, motivating high-quality TMD localization databases.

papers.title: Soluble protein analog selection engine (SPASE): An automated AI-powered server to improve protein engineering workflows.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: SPASE is an automated server integrating soluble proteinMPNN with protein-sol and Aggrescan3D plus ESMFold, generating a pool of protein variants and ranking them on predicted solubility, aggregation and folding confidence. It enriches for higher-solubility, lower-aggregation designs for engineering prioritization.

papers.title: Phase separation leads to significant conformational change in the N-terminal region of the prion protein.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry on mouse prion protein showed its unstructured N-terminal region gains stable structure as phase-separated condensates age, with beta-structure forming. Oligomeric nanoscale assemblies drive a liquid-to-solid transition and altered material properties of the condensate.

papers.title: Facile, high-throughput protein purification enabled by high-efficiency protease elution.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A novel SUMO protease construct supports rapid, high-yield protease elution during affinity chromatography, forming the keystone of an end-to-end DNA-to-protein workflow. Demonstrated on 96 mesophilic proteins and compatible with automated liquid handling, it also provides a curated dataset for machine learning.

papers.title: Total synthesis and structural characterization of a novel protein scaffold from the snail Biomphalaria glabrata.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Total chemical synthesis and X-ray crystallography of schistosomin from Biomphalaria glabrata revealed a previously undescribed disulfide-rich fold, defining a new class of miniprotein scaffold with remarkable thermal stability. Two single-residue isoforms are structurally similar; a spatial expression map across snail tissues was produced.

papers.title: Conformational asymmetry of human immunodeficiency virus-1 protease flaps increases along the darunavir drug resistance pathway.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: 19F NMR of wild-type and drug-resistant (4mut, 10mut, 11mut) HIV-1 protease showed increasing downtield shift of the W42 flap resonance as mutations accumulated. In darunavir-bound forms the W42 peak split, reflecting increasing asymmetry between the two flaps along the resistance pathway.

papers.title: GOLPH3 depletion in glioblastoma cells promotes anti-tumor effects and neuronal differentiation by affecting mTOR signaling.
papers.summary: GOLPH3 knockdown in U87MG glioblastoma cells inhibited proliferation, promoted senescence and induced a neuron-like phenotype. It reduced both mTORC1 and mTORC2 activity (decreased S6K and AKT phosphorylation), identifying a potential therapeutic vulnerability for patient-tailored glioblastoma treatment.

papers.title: Balancing cellular copper levels via the post-translational regulation of copper transport.
papers.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
papers.summary: Review of how post-translational modifications (glycosylation, phosphorylation, ubiquitination) control copper-transport proteins and their trafficking and stability, providing a mechanism by which cells sense copper deviations. Relevant to Menkes, Wilson's disease, neurodegeneration and cancer.

papers.title: Abdominal-B regulates the male seminal fluid transferome and new fecundity factors required for sperm sex peptide binding.
papers.summary: Loss of Abdominal-B in secondary cells of the Drosophila accessory gland (iab-6CocU) disrupted seminal fluid composition. Downregulation of sex peptide network proteins identified cornutus (CG1701) and hanrej (CG42564) as new factors crucial for female fecundity and dense-core granule vesicle release.

papers.title: Multi-organ single-cell transcriptomic atlas identifies QrIAA14 as a candidate negative regulator of adventitious root development in Quercus robur.
papers.summary: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of Quercus robur leaf, stem and root (41,471 cells, 30 clusters) resolved organ developmental trajectories. Auxin-signaling gene QrIAA14, enriched in root hair/cap cells, acted as a negative regulator: overexpression reduced adventitious root length ~64%, informing woody plant root regeneration.

papers.title: Characterization of METTL3/14-mediated m6A modification in human transcriptome using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing.
papers.summary: Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (RNA002/RNA004) with m6Anet and dorado profiled METTL3/14-mediated m6A at single-nucleotide resolution, validated by GLORI and miCLIP. Depletion of METTL3 vs METTL14 produced distinct transcript-specific effects, cell-type-non-redundant, with global reduction in m6A and poly(A) tail length.

papers.title: Two distributed enhancers of Sox17 additively regulate the developmental fate of bipotential ventral pancreato-biliary progenitor cells.
papers.summary: Two distributed Sox17 enhancers (Sox17E-13, Sox17E-231) additively regulate Sox17 expression. Deletions delay ventral pancreato-biliary progenitor fate conversion and reduce pancreas/gallbladder size; extrahepatic biliary structures show profound dosage sensitivity, yielding gallbladder hypoplasia, agenesis and biliary atresia.

papers.title: A Retinoic Acid-Rfx6 cascade modulates Wnt/Bmp-dependent gut tube patterning: insight into the molecular basis of Mitchell-Riley Syndrome.
papers.summary: Retinoic acid from lateral plate mesoderm directly activates Rfx6 in posterior foregut endoderm. Rfx6 promotes foregut identity while suppressing Wnt-dependent hindgut and Bmp-dependent pharyngeal fates via direct targets (Onecut1, Pdx1, Sfrp2/5, Cdx2, Nkx2-5/6). Provides mechanistic insight into Mitchell-Riley syndrome.

papers.title: FOXO6 as a Transcriptional Regulator of Hepatic Metabolic Inflammation and Hepatocarcinogenesis.
papers.summary: Review of FOXO6, a constitutively nuclear FOXO, in hepatic biology. It promotes ROS and inflammasome signaling via TXNIP, drives lipid accumulation through APOC3/PPAR-gamma activation, and in hepatocellular carcinoma associates with glycolytic metabolism, proliferation, invasion, immune suppression and reduced survival via STAT3/NF-kB/beta-catenin crosstalk.

papers.title: HDAC1/2-mediated repression of Wnt receptor expression orients asymmetric division polarity in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.summary: Seam-cell loss of the class I histone deacetylase hda-1 in C. elegans causes polarity reversals and reduced daughter-cell asymmetry in asymmetric division. HDA-1 represses Wnt receptors lin-17 and cam-1, whose opposing expression gradients orient division polarity, linking HDAC activity to graded receptor expression.

papers.title: Extracellular high mobility group box 1 as a UV-induced alarmin driving cutaneous inflammation and photoaging via TLR4 signaling.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: UV irradiation and chronic photoaging trigger active HMGB1 secretion from skin cells, driving IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8 and TNF-alpha via TLR4. HMGB1 knockdown or TLR4 blockade attenuated UV-induced cytokine expression; disrupting the axis in mice reduced neutrophil infiltration and photoaging. Target for UV skin inflammation.

papers.title: Virtual single-cell perturbation and genetic causal inference reveal CSF1R-dependent immunometabolic communication in iron metabolism-associated osteoarthritis.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: An integrative framework (machine learning, Mendelian randomization, single-cell, virtual perturbation) identified CSF1R as a central regulator of iron-metabolism-associated osteoarthritis, acting via CD14+CD16+ monocyte-macrophage remodeling. Simulated CSF1R depletion enhanced antigen processing/MHC-II/phagosome programs; overexpression activated ECM/integrin and cartilage-development pathways.

papers.title: Critical role of cellular communication network factor 1 in early osteogenesis of mesenchymal stem cells primed by low-intensity pulsed ultrasound and bone morphogenetic protein 2.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Combining low-intensity pulsed ultrasound and BMP-2 in C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells promoted CCN1 production, which regulated Runx2 expression (increased by recombinant CCN1, decreased in CCN1 knockout, rescued by CCN1 plasmid). CCN1 induced by mechanical plus osteoinductive signals plays a pivotal role in MSC osteogenesis.

papers.title: FOXO6 inhibits SMURF2-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of NR4A1 to promote retinal pigment epithelial cell ferroptosis in diabetic retinopathy.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: In diabetic retinopathy, high glucose upregulates FOXO6, which represses SMURF2 transcription; SMURF2 normally ubiquitinates and degrades NR4A1. Loss of SMURF2 raises NR4A1, promoting retinal pigment epithelial cell ferroptosis. The FOXO6-SMURF2-NR4A1 axis critically regulates ferroptosis in diabetic retinopathy.

papers.title: Differential expression of TKS4 isoforms and their role in cellular processes in breast cancer.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: TKS4 isoforms TKS4L and TKS4B were differentially expressed in breast cancer with altered tumor mRNA ratios. Six novel SH3 partners bound only TKS4L. TKS4B accumulated in the nucleus and enhanced MCF-7 migration; both isoforms promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, highlighting oncogenic targets.

papers.title: Prevotella loescheii attenuates pregnancy-induced hypertension by reshaping placental immunity and halting macrophage pyroptosis.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Prevotella loescheii attenuated pregnancy-induced hypertension by reshaping placental immunity: it reduced proteinuria and placental damage, suppressed oxidative stress and NLRP3 macrophage pyroptosis, restored Hofbauer cells and partially recovered short-chain fatty acid metabolism. Proposed as a therapeutic strategy for pregnancy-induced hypertension.

papers.title: Functional Specialization of Clathrin-Independent Endocytic Routes: Mechanisms and Cellular Roles.
papers.summary: Review of clathrin-independent endocytosis, tracing its concepts and how bacterial toxins/viruses revealed lipid- and lectin-driven internalization. The selected route dictates cargo fate (recycling, retrograde transport or degradation), modulating signaling amplitude, polarity, migration and epithelial barrier function, with an evolutionary perspective.

papers.title: Cell Type-Specific Ferroptosis Regulatory Networks in the Bone Microenvironment: Implications for the Pathogenesis and Treatment of Osteoporosis.
papers.summary: Review framing ferroptosis as a cell type-specific cell-death program in bone. It suppresses osteogenesis in osteoblasts, amplifies differentiation/inflammatory signaling in osteoclasts, acts as an early vulnerability node in osteocytes and reshapes lineage commitment in bone marrow MSCs. Proposes osteoporosis as multicellular ferroptotic dysregulation with ferroptosis-informed therapies.

papers.title: Broadening horizons: Pathogenesis and therapeutics of renal ciliopathies.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Review of renal ciliopathies, where dysregulated ciliary signaling drives cystogenesis and progression to fibrosis and renal failure. Highlights advances in prenatal diagnosis but notes challenges from incomplete molecular understanding, phenotypic overlap, genetic heterogeneity and incomplete penetrance, calling for systematic integration of signaling networks for novel therapies.

papers.title: Mechanism of Autophagic Extracellular Vesicles Revealed.
papers.summary: Commentary on autophagic extracellular vesicles (aEVs) generated from amphisomes upon autophagy induction. Molecularly and functionally distinct from exosomes, aEVs are enriched in LC3 and p62, depend on core ATG machinery, and their secretion is enhanced by autophagy, contributing to intercellular communication in viral infection.

papers.title: Shikonin promotes osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells by modulating the p38 MAPK/ETS transcription factor 1/cementum protein 1 axis in vitro.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Shikonin promoted osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells (~7.6-fold ALP, ~6.9-fold ARS at 1 uM) by activating p38 MAPK, which phosphorylates ELK1 to transcriptionally activate cementum protein 1 (CEMP1). The p38 MAPK/ELK1/CEMP1 axis mediates this effect, relevant to periodontal defect repair.

papers.title: Report on the 13th international workshop on the CCN family of genes and inaugural ARBIOCOM conference, Nice, France.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Report on the 13th international workshop on the CCN family, held within the inaugural ARBIOCOM conference in Nice. Themes included nuclear and extracellular roles of CCN proteins in gene expression, tissue development/remodeling, stem cell differentiation and disease, across skeletal, vascular, intestinal, hepatic, metabolic and cancer biology.

papers.title: The suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 regulates glioma stem cell maintenance and immune microenvironment through signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 signaling.
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of high-grade gliomas showed SOCS3 downregulated in glioma stem cells; low SOCS3 enriched TCR/p53/JAK-STAT pathways, suppressed T-cell/microglia infiltration and promoted stemness. SOCS3 overexpression reduced proliferation, induced apoptosis, suppressed neurosphere formation and STAT3/stemness markers in vitro; IL-6 reversed effects; in vivo it attenuated tumor growth and prolonged survival.

papers.title: From dysbiosis to precision oncology: translational role of the microbiome in gastrointestinal cancer.
papers.summary: Review of the gut microbiome as a regulator of GI carcinogenesis, with tumor-specific oncogenic roles for Fusobacterium nucleatum, enterotoxigenic B. fragilis, pks+ E. coli and H. pylori. Evaluates microbiome biomarkers and targeted therapies using a four-tier translational framework, and spatial/multi-omics/AI accelerators for precision oncology.

papers.title: Insights Into Aggregation-Delayed Phenotype of Dictyostelium discoideum.
papers.summary: Review of the aggregation-delayed phenotype in Dictyostelium discoideum, exploring regulatory factors beyond the key aggregation regulators (heterotrimeric G-protein signals and effectors) and highlighting the likely importance of divalent cations/ions in this phenotype caused by exposure to certain natural products.

papers.title: Sotagliflozin, a Dual SGLT1/2 Inhibitor, Modulates DNMT1 and Class I/II HDAC Expression in Association With Anticancer Effects in Breast and Lung Cancer Cells.
papers.summary: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, reduced viability, clonogenic survival, migration and invasion in MCF-7 and A549 cells with G2/M arrest and increased AMPK activation. It reduced DNMT total activity and DNMT1 and class I/II HDAC protein, plus autophagy-related changes. Preliminary evidence of epigenetic modulation, causal role unproven.

papers.title: Exposure of cells to prions induces prion strain dependent changes in mitochondrial redox state and respiration.
papers.summary: In neural cells, the 22L (but not 87V) prion strain induced changes in mitochondrial respiration and redox state independently of PrPC expression, dependent on endo-lysosomal acidification. Chronically 22L-infected cells adapted without mitochondrial dysfunction but became more susceptible to oxidative stress. Strain-dependent mitochondrial effects of prions.

papers.title: CCT8 associates with the MYO10 motor domain and regulates filopodia and breast cancer cell invasion.
papers.summary: TurboID proximity biotinylation targeted to MYO10 identified interactors; a screen found MINK1, SCRIB, CSNK1A1 and CCT8 regulate MYO10 filopodia. CCT8, a TRiC chaperonin subunit, associates with the MYO10 motor domain independently of TRiC and regulates filopodia dynamics, cell spreading, migration and invasion in breast cancer cells.

papers.title: Tumor-Associated Macrophages in the Chemoresistant Microenvironment of Gastric Cancer: Key Mechanisms and Intercellular Crosstalk.
papers.summary: Review of tumor-associated macrophages in gastric cancer chemoresistance. M2 TAMs drive resistance via CXCL5-PI3K/AKT/mTOR and TMEM-Wnt/beta-catenin; high TAM infiltration correlates with poor chemotherapy response and survival. Highlights TAM-centric therapies (checkpoint inhibitors, epigenetic modulators, combinations) to restore chemosensitivity.

papers.title: PES-8, a ZP-like protein, is required for cytoskeletal organization and contractility in the Caenorhabditis elegans spermatheca.
papers.summary: C. elegans PES-8, a zona pellucida-like protein with an extracellular ZP domain and cytoplasmic tail, localizes to the spermatheca and is essential for contractility. Loss disrupts actomyosin fiber alignment, FLN-1/filamin localization, apical junctions and calcium signaling, preventing oocyte transit. Regulates cytoskeletal organization and calcium-mediated contraction.

papers.title: Guarding the integrity of cell-based research: the role of the ICLAC Register of Misidentified Cell Lines.
papers.summary: Commentary on the ICLAC Register of Misidentified Cell Lines (version 14 now released) as a curated open resource to identify cell lines not representing their claimed origin. Encourages consulting the register before acquisition and authenticating cultures (STR profiling) at defined checkpoints to improve reproducibility of cell-based research.

papers.title: Tet Trim-Away: a conditional rapid protein degradation system for Tetrahymena thermophila.
papers.summary: Tet Trim-Away adapts TRIM-away for Tetrahymena thermophila, fusing TRIM21 RBCC domains with an anti-mCherry nanobody degron under an inducible promoter. It depletes target proteins within ~30 minutes, is reversible, functions across cellular compartments and produces loss-of-function phenotypes, enabling acute protein depletion.

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome for the spotted flying dragon (Draco maculatus).
papers.summary: A chromosome-level assembly of the spotted flying dragon Draco maculatus (1.73 Gb, scaffold N50 255.5 Mb, 18,805 annotated genes) anchored to 17 pseudochromosomes, the first nuclear genome for flying dragons. Includes transcriptomic data from patagium, skin and four internal tissues, informing adaptive gliding.

papers.title: Binocular combination in the autonomic nervous system.
papers.summary: Using a novel binocular multiprimary system with silent substitution, luminance and S-cone pupil responses showed binocular facilitation, melanopsin responses were invariant to eye number, and the L-M pathway showed binocular inhibition. Results support a Bayesian model with pathway-specific interocular suppression weights and differing response lags.

papers.title: Association of MDM2 rs2279744 and rs937282 polymorphisms with breast cancer susceptibility and circulating MDM2 and p53 levels in Bangladeshi women: A case-control study.
papers.summary: Case-control study in Bangladeshi women: heterozygous TG genotype of MDM2 rs2279744 associated with increased breast cancer risk, GG protective; rs937282 not associated. Circulating MDM2 was elevated in patients and varied by genotype, with inverse p53 correlation; MDM2 high in HER2+/triple-positive subtypes. No functional validation limits causal inference.

papers.title: A cross-sectional validation study of the verran and snyder-halpern sleep scale and the factors influencing sleep questionnaire in Dutch hospitals.
papers.summary: Cross-cultural validation of the Verran and Snyder-Halpern sleep scale and factors-influencing-sleep questionnaire in 693 Dutch hospital patients; CFA yielded a three-factor (VSH) and one-factor (FISQ) model. Over half reported poorer sleep than home; daytime sleep linked to more disturbance and lower effectiveness.

papers.title: Identifying DNA mutations in Sepia, White, Yellow, and Vestigial genes in D. melanogaster - Integrating inquiry-based experiential learning into undergraduate Genetics Laboratory curriculum.
papers.summary: An undergraduate Drosophila genetics laboratory integrated inquiry-based learning in which students identified DNA mutations in sepia, white, yellow and vestigial genes underlying eye, body and wing phenotypes. Surveys showed students valued hands-on amplification/cloning, experimental design and real-world connections, supporting research experiences.

papers.title: Brown and white adipocyte like cells derived exosomes differentially regulate stemness, hormone secretion, apoptosis, and lipid metabolism in model cells.
papers.summary: Brown vs white adipocyte-like cell exosomes differentially regulated stemness, hormone secretion, apoptosis and lipid metabolism in model cells. BALC-derived exosomes increased estradiol secretion and promoted osteogenic differentiation while reducing stemness markers OCT4/SOX2; they also drove the most differentially expressed lipids and lipid storage/membrane remodeling.

papers.title: Annona crassiflora seed extract modulates histological and molecular markers associated with prostate cancer progression in TRAMP mice.
papers.summary: Araticum (Annona crassiflora) seed extract in TRAMP mice delayed progression of premalignant/malignant prostate lesions and preserved tissue, with antiproliferative activity (reduced PCNA, IGF-1R, AR), suppressed TLR/NF-kB/TNF-alpha inflammatory signaling, reduced Bcl-2 and promoted caspase activation. Suggested as a chemopreventive agent in combination therapy.

papers.title: Revising NHE-1: From Cardiac Homeostasis to Heart Failure and Future Drug Development.
papers.summary: Review of NHE-1, a Na+/H+ exchanger, in cardiac cells: it maintains pH and couples to Na+/Ca2+ exchange and mitochondrial ion handling. Sustained activation promotes Na+ accumulation, Ca2+ overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, arrhythmias and fibrosis. Clinical trials failed; SGLT2 inhibitors act indirectly; new approaches target regulatory sites rather than the transport pore.

papers.title: Interactions Between E3 Ubiquitin Ligases and Deubiquitinases in AKT Regulation: Implications in Skeletal Muscle Homeostasis.
papers.summary: Systematic review identifies four E3 ligase-deubiquitinase pairs regulating AKT in skeletal muscle: TRAF6-CYLD, MUL1-USP9X, CHIP-UCH37 and SCF-SKP2-USP37, all through non-catalytic interfaces. Evidence is uneven across pairs; the latter three are testable hypotheses. Recasts AKT ubiquitination as a complex-centric integrator relevant to sarcopenia.

papers.title: Dual facets of copper in the malignant transformation of oral submucous fibrosis: A narrative review.
papers.summary: Review of copper in oral submucous fibrosis and its malignant transformation. Copper increases lysyl oxidase activity (collagen cross-linking); excess copper drives oxidative stress favoring transformation, while moderate elevations promote proliferation and angiogenesis in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Copper is context-dependent: pro-fibrotic at moderate, cytotoxic at higher concentrations.

papers.title: Regulated cell death in autoimmune diseases: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.summary: Review of non-classical regulated cell death pathways (ferroptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, panoptosis, NETosis, parthanatos, cuproptosis) in autoimmune diseases. Unlike apoptosis these are pro-inflammatory, releasing DAMPs, cytokines and autoantigens; dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation and impaired tolerance. Discusses therapeutic targeting of major RCD regulators.

papers.title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals a novel frameshift and a recurrent nonsense SPG11 variant causing rare familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 5 in two consanguineous Pakistani families.
papers.summary: Whole-exome sequencing of five juvenile-onset (before age 25) autosomal-recessive ALS patients from two consanguineous Pakistani families identified homozygous SPG11 variants: a novel frameshift (c.6738dup, p.Glu2247Ter) and a recurrent nonsense (c.782C>A, p.Ser261Ter). Findings show overlapping phenotypes between SPG11-related juvenile ALS and hereditary spastic paraplegia.

papers.title: Wing Shape and Color Pattern Modifications in Giant Silk Moths Using Sulfated Polysaccharides: Understanding Morphogenic Signals in Pupal Wings of Lepidoptera.
papers.summary: Heparin (a Wnt/Wingless agonist) and dextran sulfate (antagonist) consistently altered wing shape and eyespot/tail patterns in luna and polyphemus moths, expanding or contracting hindwing tails and eyespots. This provides a framework for investigating morphogenic signals in pupal wings and links wing morphology to evolution and flight.

papers.title: Two Paralogues as They Like It: Conserved and Divergent Evolution of Vertebrate Gcm Genes.
papers.summary: Comparative analysis of Gcm1/Gcm2 expression revealed conserved expression in gill epithelia across cartilaginous fishes, non-teleost actinopterygians and amphibians, with overlapping but distinct patterns. Gcm1 further showed lineage-specific expression, including external gills and yolk-sac epithelial cells with vacuole-like cytoplasm, indicating distinct evolutionary trajectories.

papers.title: Patterns of Autonomous and Conditional Neural Specification for the Brain and Ventral Nerve Cord in Annelida.
papers.summary: Blastomere isolation/ablation in two annelids (Capitella teleta, Platynereis dumerilii) showed autonomous specification of anterior neural tissue in 1q micromeres and intrinsic trunk neural fate in 2D. In C. teleta additional proneural/anti-neural signals regulate trunk fate, decoupled from dorsal-ventral axis formation, with conserved head/trunk specification mechanisms.

papers.title: Supraphysiological 25-Hydroxyvitamin D(3) and Calcipotriol Induce Reactive Oxygen Species, Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Apoptosis in HeLa Cervical Cancer Cells.
papers.summary: In HeLa cervical cancer cells, supraphysiological 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 and calcipotriol reduced viability and induced apoptosis (annexin V, caspase-3/7), with increased ROS-positive populations, mitochondrial depolarization, decreased catalase/SOD, and reduced MAPK, PI3K/AKT and NF-kB pro-survival proteins. NAC partially attenuated calcipotriol effects without establishing ROS as a necessary mediator.

papers.title: Genome-wide cyclin gene evolution in Arabidopsis and Brassica reveals polyploidization-driven duplication and flowering-time associations.
papers.summary: Genome-wide analysis of 1,087 cyclin genes (23 types) across ten Brassicaceae genomes showed expansion driven strongly by polyploidization, with whole-genome duplication predominant and highest duplication frequency in Brassica juncea. Pan-genomic and flowering-time analyses identified Bna21CYCA2 and Bna113CYCD4 as candidate flowering-time variants.

papers.title: Dual antitumor and neuroprotective activities of lipid ether amide hybrids in glioma cells and metabolically damaged neurons.
papers.summary: Oleic- and palmitic-acid propranolol ether (LEA) hybrids inhibited clonal growth of patient-derived glioma stem/progenitor cells at low-micromolar IC50 without toxicity to normal cortex, and increased survival and restored architecture of metabolically stressed neurons. Docking showed nanomolar binding to GPR3/6 and micromolar to TLX, a dual antitumor/neuroprotective lipid class.

papers.title: LNP-mediated silencing of oncogenic lncRNA PVT1 enhances chemotherapeutic efficacy in osteosarcoma.
papers.summary: PVT1 was upregulated in osteosarcoma cell lines/tissues. Lipid nanoparticles (~100 nm) encapsulating siPVT1 suppressed PVT1, reduced viability (IC50 29.30 nM) and induced apoptosis, with synergism when combined with doxorubicin or sorafenib. In a humanized mouse xenograft model, LNP-siPVT1 plus doxorubicin inhibited tumor growth without overt toxicity.

papers.title: Surface protein profiling reveals depot-specific features of subcutaneous and visceral adipose progenitor cells.
papers.summary: Subcutaneous adipose progenitor cells showed elevated galectin-9, CD44 and CD63 versus visceral cells. Galectin-9 promotes an anti-inflammatory phenotype, CD44 quantitatively modulates adipogenic differentiation, and CD63 enhances exosome release and resistance to iron-induced stress. Surface protein signatures distinguish depots and link to metabolic disease susceptibility.

papers.title: Exploring the sex-dependent effects of midnolin loss on hepatic transcription and chromatin accessibility.
papers.summary: Liver-specific Midn (gene-trap) mice showed sex-dependent transcriptional changes: males had prominent lipid-associated changes (fatty acid biosynthesis, steroid, retinoic acid and bile acid metabolism) while females had few coherent metabolic changes. ATAC-seq revealed modest chromatin-accessibility changes with nuclear-receptor motif enrichment, suggesting sex-dependent Midn roles in liver homeostasis.

papers.title: Dose-dependent protective effects of p-coumaric acid on testicular ischemia/reperfusion injury in a mouse model of testicular torsion.
papers.summary: In a mouse testicular torsion/detorsion model, p-coumaric acid (100 and 200 mg/kg, but not 50) dose-dependently improved sperm quality and kinematics, boosted antioxidant defenses (TAC, SOD, GPX), preserved seminiferous tubule architecture and suppressed apoptosis, protecting fertility against ischemia/reperfusion injury.

papers.title: Inferring feedback regulation from static snapshots of a single signal.
papers.summary: AOF (Assay of Feedback) infers the sign, magnitude and state-dependence of feedback from fixed-cell snapshots using ergodic rate analysis, without circuit perturbations. Applied to AKT phosphorylation across the cell cycle, it unmasked a localized negative-feedback loop at G1/S, likely an mTORC1/S6K1-dependent inhibitory IRS1 phosphorylation.

papers.title: NAD(+) metabolism influences TGF-β-associated transcriptional programs and the gut microbiota in murine models of colitis.
papers.summary: NMN restored subsets of TGF-beta-associated transcriptional changes in mouse embryonic fibroblasts and affected fibrosis genes (nt5e, enpp1). In a DSS colitis model, NMN increased regeneration genes and reduced fibrosis/immune pathways, altered gut microbiota and TGF-beta/IgA immune signatures. Associations support a role for NAD+ metabolism in colitis prevention approaches.

papers.title: The NtAN3 gene plays a key role in increasing tobacco leaf area.
papers.summary: NtAN3 regulates tobacco leaf area: overexpression increased and silencing decreased leaf area by positively modulating leaf cell proliferation and expansion at early developmental stages. Transcriptomics revealed altered carbohydrate metabolism (starch, sucrose, galactose) and identified late-response genes, providing molecular references for high-yield tobacco breeding.

papers.title: Application and prospect of zinc oxide nanoparticle-enhanced biomimetic hydrogels in articular cartilage repair.
papers.summary: Review of zinc oxide nanoparticle-enhanced biomimetic hydrogels for articular cartilage repair. ZnO NPs improve hydrogel mechanical stability and provide antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and chondrogenic benefits via controlled Zn2+ release. Summarizes construction strategies and in vitro/in vivo evidence, while highlighting biosafety, concentration control and translational challenges.

papers.title: System level identification and multidimensional analysis of hub genes reveal complex regulatory networks underlying human iPSC differentiation into motor neurons.
papers.summary: Integrated bioinformatics of a day-28 iPSC-to-motor-neuron dataset identified 15 hub genes (BUB1, TOP2A, AURKB, CCNA2, TP53) in cell-cycle/mitotic programs; GO/KEGG highlighted cell cycle, DNA replication, senescence, p53 signaling; cytocluster modules and 5,316 miRNA-mRNA pairs were mapped. Codon-usage analysis indicated translational optimization. Requires experimental validation.

papers.title: Virus-like particles vaccine of porcine epidemic diarrhea virus spike 1 protein induces protective immunity challenge in piglets.
papers.summary: Recombinant S1-ferritin virus-like particles (S1-F-VLP, via SpyTag-SpyCatcher) were safe and induced high serum IgG, IgA and neutralizing antibodies in mice, sows and piglets. In challenged piglets, vaccination lowered diarrhea score, intestinal viral load and pathological damage, indicating S1-F-VLP as a promising PEDV vaccine candidate.

papers.title: Coronary endothelial cells receive Notch1 signal during heart development.
papers.summary: Re-analysis of human and mouse single-cell RNA-seq plus transgenic Notch1 lineage tracing (Gal4/UAS and Cre/LoxP) showed coronary endothelial cells, and a small proportion of endocardial cells, received Notch1 signal during heart development. Ongoing signaling was seen in vascular lumen-lining cells. Clarifies Notch1-receiving lineages and congenital heart disease.

papers.title: Processing enhances the anti-hepatocellular carcinoma effect of Momordicae Semen via remodeling chemical composition and regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 pathway.
papers.summary: Processing altered Momordicae Semen chemical composition (41 constituents identified). Methyl gypsogenin 3-O-beta-D-glucuronopyranoside (MG) bound Akt/mTOR/STAT3 pathway proteins; processed MS at high dose alleviated liver injury, suppressed inflammatory cytokines, reduced Ki67 and inhibited Akt/mTOR/STAT3 phosphorylation in a DEN-induced rat HCC model, with superior efficacy to crude MS.
